name: Mancala
intro: Learn Mancala (Kalah) in minutes: sowing seeds, free turns, captures and the end of the game, then the planning that wins: chaining free turns and protecting your seeds.

ladder.name: Mira
ladder.blurb: Takes every free turn and capture she sees.

ladder.name: The Monocle
ladder.blurb: Plans long chains. Guards every pit.

units.name: How Mancala works
units.blurb: The board, sowing, free turns, captures and the end of the game.

lessons.title: The Mancala board and how to set it up
lessons.summary: How to set up a Mancala board: six pits each, four seeds in every pit, and a store at each end. Learn which side and store are yours.
lessons.wrap: That’s the board. Next: how to move, which in Mancala is called sowing.

steps.text:
Mancala is played on a board with two rows of six pits and a large store at each end. The version here is Kalah, the most popular one.

Each pit starts with 4 seeds, 48 in all. The stores start empty.

The bottom row is yours, and so is the store on your right. Your opponent has the top row and the store on the left.

The goal: get more seeds into your store than your opponent.
Quick check.
steps.prompt: Which store is yours?
steps.explain: The one on your right, at the end of your row. Seeds travel towards it.

lessons.title: How to move in Mancala: sowing seeds
lessons.summary: In Mancala you pick up every seed from one of your pits and sow them one at a time around the board. Learn sowing with practice.
lessons.wrap: Pick up, then drop one at a time, anticlockwise. Next: the free turn.

steps.text:
On your turn, pick up all the seeds from one of your pits. Then drop them one at a time into the next pits, moving anticlockwise: right along your row, into your store, then along your opponent’s row.

Watch the first pit being sown.
Pits are numbered 1 to 6 from left to right.
steps.prompt: Sow the seeds from your second pit.
steps.wrong: Pick the second pit from the left.
steps.done: Four seeds, one into each of the next four pits.

steps.text: Seeds that pass your store carry on into your opponent’s pits. That’s allowed: they just aren’t yours any more.
steps.prompt: Your last pit has 4 seeds. Tap the pit where its last seed would land.
steps.wrong: Count again: one into your store, then three along the top row, going right to left.
steps.done: Right: store, then three pits along the top.

steps.text: One more rule: you skip your opponent’s store when sowing, but you always drop a seed in yours.
steps.prompt: Can you sow a seed into your opponent’s store?
steps.explain: No. You skip it, so seeds only ever reach a store by its owner’s sowing.

lessons.title: Mancala free turns: landing in your store
lessons.summary: If your last seed lands in your own store, you get another turn. Learn to spot free turns in Mancala by counting seeds.
lessons.wrap: Count the seeds: a pit with exactly enough to reach your store gives a free turn. Next: captures.

steps.text: If the last seed you sow lands in your store, you get a free turn: you go again straight away.
Count the steps from each pit to your store. Which pit has exactly the right number of seeds?
steps.prompt: Make a move that earns a free turn.
steps.wrong: The last seed didn’t reach your store. Count again: you need a pit whose seeds run out exactly in the store.
steps.done: Free turn! That’s the best possible first move.

steps.text: The trick is to count: pit 6 needs 1 seed to reach the store, pit 5 needs 2, and so on.
steps.prompt: How many seeds does pit 2 need to end in your store?
steps.explain: 5: one each into pits 3, 4, 5 and 6, and the fifth into the store.

lessons.title: Captures in Mancala
lessons.summary: If your last seed lands in an empty pit on your side, you capture it and every seed in the pit opposite. Learn Mancala captures.
lessons.wrap: Empty pits on your side are capture traps, for you and against you. Next: how the game ends.

steps.text:
If your last seed lands in an empty pit on your side, you capture: that seed and every seed in the opposite pit go into your store.

Your pit 3 is empty, and the pit opposite has 6 seeds.
Which pit’s seeds would end exactly in pit 3?
steps.prompt: Make the capture.
steps.wrong: No capture. You need your last seed to land in your empty pit 3.

steps.text: Your opponent can do exactly the same to you.
steps.prompt: Your pit 4 has 9 seeds and the pit opposite is empty. Is that dangerous?
options: Yes, if your opponent can land a last seed there
steps.explain: Yes. If they can end a sowing in that empty pit, they take all 9 of yours.

lessons.title: How a game of Mancala ends
lessons.summary: Mancala ends when one player’s six pits are all empty. The other player keeps the seeds left on their side. Learn the ending rule.
lessons.wrap: You know every rule of Mancala. Test yourself in the rules check.

steps.text:
The game ends when all six pits on one side are empty. The other player then puts every seed left on their side into their own store.

The player with more seeds in their store wins.
You have one seed left, in pit 6. Playing it puts it in your store, and your side is empty.
steps.prompt: If the game ends then, who wins?
steps.explain: Your opponent: they keep the 7 seeds still on their side, so 20 + 7 = 27.

steps.text: Here you have no choice: it’s your only move.
steps.prompt: Play your last seed.
steps.done: Game over. Lesson: count both sides before ending the game.

units.name: Rules check
units.blurb: Prove you know the rules, then move on to strategy.

lessons.title: Mancala rules quiz
lessons.summary: Test your knowledge of the Mancala rules: sowing, skipping the opponent’s store, free turns, captures and how the game ends.
lessons.wrap: Rules check passed. Now learn to plan ahead.

steps.text: Question 1.
steps.prompt: Which way do seeds travel?
steps.explain: Anticlockwise: along your row towards your store.

steps.text: Question 2.
steps.prompt: Take a free turn.
steps.done: Pit 3: four seeds, last one in the store.

steps.text: Question 3.
steps.prompt: Your last seed lands in an empty pit on your opponent’s side. What happens?
options: Nothing: captures only happen on your side
steps.explain: Nothing. Captures only happen in empty pits on your own side.

steps.text: Question 4.
steps.prompt: Make a capture.

steps.text: Question 5.
steps.prompt: One player’s pits are all empty. What happens to the seeds left on the other side?
options: They go to the player whose side they’re on
steps.explain: They go into the store of the player whose side they’re on.

units.name: Planning ahead
units.blurb: Chain free turns together and keep your seeds safe.

lessons.title: Chaining free turns in Mancala
lessons.summary: Strong Mancala players chain free turns together, playing the pits nearest the store first. Practise a four-move chain.
lessons.wrap: Play the free turn closest to your store first, so it doesn’t spoil the others.

steps.text:
Several pits here can give a free turn. The order matters: sowing from a pit far from your store adds seeds to the pits nearer it and spoils their count.

Rule of thumb: play the free turn closest to your store first.
Pit 6 (1 seed) and pit 5 (2 seeds) both reach the store.
steps.prompt: Start the chain with the right free turn.
steps.wrong: That breaks the chain. Start with the pit nearest your store.

steps.text: Pit 5 still has exactly 2 seeds.
steps.prompt: Take the next free turn.
steps.wrong: Pit 5 is the one that ends in your store now.

steps.text: Count again: pit 3 has 4 seeds, and it’s 4 steps from your store.
steps.prompt: Take a third free turn.
steps.wrong: Find the pit whose seeds end exactly in your store.
steps.done: Three free turns in a row.

steps.text: No free turn left, but pit 5 is now empty, and the pit opposite has seeds.
steps.prompt: Finish with a capture.
steps.wrong: Look for a single seed that lands in your empty pit 5.
steps.done: Three free turns and a capture. That’s how strong players move.

lessons.title: Protecting your seeds in Mancala
lessons.summary: A big pit with an empty pit opposite is a target. Learn to see your opponent’s capture threats and move your seeds to safety.
lessons.wrap: After every move, look at your opponent’s side: can they land in an empty pit across from your seeds? That completes the Mancala path: time for the ladder.

steps.text:
Your pit 4 has 8 seeds. The pit opposite is empty, and your opponent has a single seed right next to it.

On their turn they can sow that seed into the empty pit and capture your 8.
You have small captures on offer, but grabbing 3 seeds and losing 9 is a bad deal.
steps.prompt: Make the move that removes the threat.
steps.wrong: That leaves your 8 seeds open to capture. Move them out of danger.
steps.done: Safe. Your seeds are spread out, and the empty pit opposite is filled too.
